question: Measuring from the closest point of each object, which of these objects (chair, bed, pillow, lamp) is the closest to the microwave?
Measuring from the closest point of each object, which of these objects (window, chair, door, washing machine) is the closest to the radiator?
Measuring from the closest point of each object, which of these objects (stove, chair, refrigerator, table) is the closest to the tv?
If I am standing by the ceiling light and facing the toilet, is the door to the left or the right of the toilet?
If I am standing by the bookshelf and facing the door, is the refrigerator to the left or the right of the door?
If I am standing by the stove and facing the table, is the refrigerator to the left or the right of the table?

If I am standing by the window and facing the lamp, is the door to my left, right, or back?
An object is to my back if I would have to turn at least 135 degrees in order to face it.

If I am standing by the bed and facing the chair, is the mirror to my left, right, or back?
An object is to my back if I would have to turn at least 135 degrees in order to face it.

If I am standing by the refrigerator and facing the microwave, is the ceiling light to my left, right, or back?
An object is to my back if I would have to turn at least 135 degrees in order to face it.

If I am standing by the tv and facing the bed, is the chair to my front-left, front-right, back-left, or back-right?
The directions refer to the quadrants of a Cartesian plane (if I am standing at the origin and facing along the positive y-axis).
